RadioStatus.Tune.Help: Keys PTT and transmits a steady test tone at the given frequency/duration so the other station's AFC/tuning indicator can lock on -- does not send an image.

RadioStatus.FrequencyReadout.Help: Click to enter a frequency directly.
RadioStatus.Error.TuneFailed: Tune failed. Check your radio and audio device settings.

RadioStatus.Error.InvalidPresetBandwidth: Favourite "{0}" has an invalid filter bandwidth -- enter a value between 50 and 20000 Hz before saving.

RadioStatus.Error.ModeNotSupported: This radio has no equivalent for that mode.
RadioStatus.Error.ModeRejected: The radio rejected that mode change: {0}
RadioStatus.Warning.RxMaintenanceApproac: RX has been continuously active for a long time without a pause -- it will restart automatically once idle, or be force-stopped soon if it never idles.
RadioStatus.Error.RxMaintenanceRequired: RX was stopped for required internal maintenance. Click Receiving to resume.
RadioStatus.SsbAsPkt.Help: When checked, the USB/LSB buttons target the rig's PKTUSB/PKTLSB (data) modes instead of plain voice USB/LSB. If the rig is currently on USB or LSB, it converts immediately.
RadioStatus.BandwidthInput.Help: Requests this filter passband (Hz) from the rig. An overly narrow value can break SSTV decode or clip TX audio -- the rig may also silently snap it to its nearest real filter.
RadioStatus.FavouritesHint: Click a preset to recall it
RadioStatus.ReceivingPausedForTx.Help: Capture is briefly paused while transmitting -- listening resumes automatically once the transmission finishes.
Panes.RxImage.AutoDetect.Help: Listening: the decoder actively searches for and decodes incoming pictures. Paused: it stops searching -- the waterfall keeps scrolling, but the signal-level meter and station-ID decode pause too, until you resume. Forcing a specific mode with a quick-mode button below automatically resumes.
Panes.RxImage.ModeOverride.Help: The decoder always auto-detects mode from the VIS header. There is no persistent mode lock -- use a quick-mode button below to force the next decode into a specific mode.
Panes.RxImage.QuickMode.ReassignHint: Right-click to reassign this slot or hold its mode
Panes.RxImage.QuickMode.HoldingHelp: Every future reception decodes as this mode, ignoring what the sender's own VIS header actually says, until released. It does not change the mode already being decoded right now.
Panes.RxImage.Error.RecordFailed: Could not start or stop recording.
Panes.RxInput.Bpf.Help: How tightly the receiver band-pass filters incoming audio before demodulation. Normal disables this band-pass filter entirely. Wide is the recommended default. Sharp and Very sharp reject more adjacent-tone interference at the cost of more sensitivity to frequency drift. If a reception is in progress, a change queues and takes effect once that reception ends, not mid-image.
Panes.RxInput.NotchTooltip: Suppresses a narrow band around the tuned frequency before decoding. Click the spectrum trace to tune. The spectrum/waterfall display does not visually show its effect.
Panes.RxDsp.AfcTooltip: Automatic frequency control. Corrects a tuning offset by measuring the sync tone and shifting the decode back toward nominal. Switching it off applies during the current image: the correction stops being added from the next line onward and the tone detectors return to their nominal frequencies. Pixels already decoded keep the correction they were given. With AFC off, the Signal quality card's Sync tone row shows “—”, because no correction is being measured. AVT mode never uses AFC, whatever this is set to.
Panes.RxFrameMeta.LookupQrz.Help: Needs a callsign above and QRZ.com lookup configured in Options > QRZ.com.

Macros.Title: Macros
Macros.Token.Name: The operator's own configured name.
Macros.Token.Grid: The operator's own configured Maidenhead grid square.
Macros.Token.Frequency: The radio's currently tuned frequency. Only resolves with a live radio connection -- shows blank in this preview.
Macros.Token.Mode: The radio's currently selected mode. Only resolves with a live radio connection -- shows blank in this preview.
Macros.Token.Distance: Distance to the "his_grid" template variable, if set. Only resolves inside the TX image editor's own template designer -- shows blank in this preview.
Macros.Token.Bearing: Bearing to the "his_grid" template variable, if set. Only resolves inside the TX image editor's own template designer -- shows blank in this preview.
Macros.VariablesExplanation: Any other {word} used in a text element -- not just the examples below -- automatically adds a fill-in row to the TX editor's QSO FILL bar. It resolves fresh each time the card is sent, never baked in while editing. Left unfilled, it appears verbatim as {word} on the transmitted image -- unlike the tokens above, which either resolve or show blank. Distance and Bearing above read whatever value is supplied in a his_grid row specifically.
Macros.Variables.HisCall: The other station's callsign. Supplied via the QSO FILL bar, or pre-filled automatically when copying a received image to TX.
Macros.Variables.HisGrid: The other station's grid square. Also feeds Distance/Bearing above. Supplied via the QSO FILL bar, or pre-filled automatically when copying a received image to TX.
Macros.Variables.Rsv: A free-form per-QSO field (signal report, a note, anything else) -- supplied via the QSO FILL bar.
Panes.TxControls.BackgroundHelp: Loads a background photo — the base image for this transmission. It replaces any current background and is not saved with templates. To save a fixed photo as part of a reusable template design, use "Turn into backdrop" in the editor's own canvas right-click menu.
Panes.TxControls.AutoFollowRxMode: Auto-set TX mode from received signal
Panes.TxControls.AutoFollowRxMode.Help: Auto: TX mode automatically matches the last mode received, so you reply in kind -- except while transmitting, or when the received mode's picture width doesn't match the image already loaded for TX. Manual: TX mode stays at whatever you pick yourself.
Panes.TxControls.Error.LoadFailed: Could not load that image file.
Panes.TxControls.Error.TransmitFailed: Transmission failed. Check your radio and audio device settings.
Panes.TxControls.Error.SwrCutoff: Transmission stopped automatically: SWR too high.
Panes.TxControls.VoxToneLabel.Help: Legacy's fixed pre-VIS leader-tone burst, sent before every transmission. Not the same as legacy's separate, unported VOX feature (a user-editable custom tone sequence, used to prime an external VOX-activated transmitter/relay before the burst).
Panes.TxImageEditor.LockAspectToMode.Hel: Constrains the crop rectangle to the selected mode's own aspect ratio. Combine with Preserve aspect OFF to fill the frame edge-to-edge with no distortion and no letterboxing.

Panes.TxImageEditor.GrowToFillEnabledHin: Let the font grow larger than its set size when the box has room, not just shrink to fit. Off by default; the toggle itself resets when the template reloads, but the grown size is saved and reloads at its actual grown size, not its original set size.
Panes.TxImageEditor.Caption: Preview shows crop/scale/overlay placement only -- does not simulate per-mode color/chroma effects.
Panes.TxImageEditor.SetAsBackdrop.Help: Saved with the template — the background photo is not.
Panes.TxImageEditor.PromoteBackgroundToB: Saves the current background photo as a locked backdrop element, so it's included when you save this as a template. The background becomes blank.

Options.Title: Options
Options.Apply.Help: Saves every change in this dialog without closing it.
Options.Cancel.Help: Closes without saving anything changed since the last Save, Apply, or Connect.
Options.ResetAll.ConfirmPrompt: This resets every setting below to its default. Nothing is saved until you click Save, but this can't be undone within this dialog. Continue?
Options.Appearance.DecodingIndicatorBlin: Blink while an image is decoding
Options.Audio.SampleRate.Help: Whole-Hz DSP rate from 5000 to 48500. Applies live on Save, no restart needed. If receiving, this briefly reopens the capture device and ends any reception in progress. 11025 Hz is the legacy default.
Options.Audio.TxSampleRateOffset.Help: Manual correction (Hz, -1500 to 1500) for your sound card's real TX clock drift from the Sample rate above -- applied to transmitted tone generation only, never to the sample rate itself. Leave at 0 unless you've measured a real drift (e.g. another station reports your signal sounds slightly fast or slow).
Options.Radio.Backend.Help: How Scanline Studio talks to your radio. 'None' disables frequency/mode/PTT control entirely. 'rigctld' connects to an already-running Hamlib rigctld process (or compatible), which can control almost any rig Hamlib supports. 'Linked Hamlib' talks to a system-installed libhamlib directly, no separate daemon process needed, but requires libhamlib to actually be installed on this machine.
Options.Radio.Connect.Help: Connects the app's real radio session, saving any changes above first. Takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
Options.Radio.Disconnect.Help: Disconnects the app's real radio session.
Options.Radio.Connect.Help.None: Select a backend above first -- there is nothing to connect to with "None".
Options.Radio.Connect.GaveUp.Title: Radio disconnected
Options.Radio.Hamlib.LibraryPath.Help: Path to a specific Hamlib shared library file. Leave blank to let Scanline Studio search the usual system locations for it.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.LibraryPath.Caption: Applies live on Save -- an already-open Hamlib connection keeps using the previous library until it reconnects.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.Probe.FoundNoModels: Found Hamlib {0} at {1}, but could not list its rig models. Enter the rig model number manually below.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.RigList.Placeholder: Browse or auto-detect Hamlib above to list its rig models
Options.Radio.Hamlib.Model.Help: Hamlib's own numeric rig model ID (rig_model_t) -- look it up with 'rigctl -l' or Hamlib's own rig list. There is no Scanline Studio rig database; this must be Hamlib's own model number.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.SerialPort.Help: The serial device your rig is connected to for CAT control, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux or COM3 on Windows.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.PttType.Help: How Scanline Studio keys your transmitter. VOX: no command is sent at all -- your rig's own hardware VOX keys on audio presence. CAT: keyed over the same CAT connection as frequency/mode control. RTS/DTR: keyed by asserting a serial control line, using the PTT port below.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.PttPort.Help: The serial device that keys PTT via RTS/DTR -- separate from the CAT serial port above, since some setups use a dedicated PTT cable/adapter. Only used for the RTS/DTR PTT methods.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.TestPtt.VoxDisabled: Keys PTT for up to 5 seconds so you can confirm it actually keys your rig (an LED, a relay click). Disabled for VOX, since Hamlib sends no command at all for it -- there's nothing to test; the rig keys itself on audio presence.
Options.Radio.Hamlib.AlreadyConnected: Disconnect the active radio connection first -- a test can't run alongside it.
Options.Radio.Flrig.AlreadyConnected: Disconnect the active radio connection first -- a test can't run alongside it.
Options.Radio.OmniRig.AlreadyConnected: Disconnect the active radio connection first -- a test can't run alongside it.
Options.Radio.Tune.Help: Keys PTT and transmits a steady test tone for up to 30 seconds -- drag Pwr while it plays and watch your radio's own power meter until it reads the output you want, then click Stop tune (or wait for the 30s safety cutoff).
Options.Radio.SwrCutoffEnabled: Stop TX if SWR too high
Options.Radio.SwrCutoffEnabled.Help: Cancels an in-progress transmit if your connected rig reports SWR above the threshold below for two consecutive readings. A convenience backstop riding this app's own ~250ms poll cadence -- not a substitute for your rig's own hardware SWR protection.
Options.Radio.SwrCutoffCapabilityHint: Your connected radio/backend does not report SWR -- this cutoff will not fire.
Options.Tx.Callsign.Help: Your own callsign. Used in the TX overlay editor's %m macro token ("MY CALL" insert-field chip), CW-ID text, FSK station ID, and QSO log export.
Options.Tx.DefaultRst.Help: Prefills the RST Sent/Received fields when you log a new QSO. SSTV operators exchange R-S-V (Readability/Strength/Video) and near-universally report 595, not ham radio's classic 599 -- clear this field to prefill nothing instead.
Options.NotImplemented.Help: Not yet implemented -- tracked on the roadmap. This control is disabled and has no effect yet.
Options.General.JpegQuality.Help: 1-100 JPEG compression quality used when manually exporting a received frame as JPEG (Gallery tab's Export button). Received images are always auto-saved as PNG regardless of this setting -- it only applies when you choose JPEG in the export dialog.

Options.General.Storage.Audio.Label: Auto-save RX audio
Options.General.Storage.Audio.Caption: Applies immediately. Saves each reception's raw audio alongside its image. Existing audio files are not moved -- only new receptions are saved here.

Options.Audio.StereoSource.Help: Which channel to decode from when the capture device is stereo -- mono mixes both, Left/Right uses only that channel (useful when RX and a second signal share one stereo input).
Options.Audio.StereoTx: Send TX audio to both stereo channels separately
Options.Radio.Backend.OmniRig.Help: Talks to an already-running OmniRig instance (or launches OmniRig if none is running) as a client, letting Scanline Studio share the rig with another OmniRig-aware application (e.g. a logger). Windows-only.
Options.Radio.Backend.OmniRig.Help.NotWi: OmniRig is a Windows-only COM automation server -- unavailable on this operating system.
Options.Radio.Backend.FlRig.Help: Talks to an already-running flrig instance as a client over its XML-RPC interface.
Options.Decode.SenseLevel.Help: How strong a signal needs to be before the decoder treats it as real SSTV rather than noise. Higher = less sensitive, fewer false decodes on a noisy band.
Options.Decode.RxBpf.Help: How tightly the receiver band-pass filters incoming audio before demodulation. Normal disables this band-pass filter entirely. Wide is the recommended default. Sharp and Very sharp reject more adjacent-tone interference at the cost of more sensitivity to frequency drift. Applies live on Save; if a reception is in progress, it queues and takes effect once that reception ends, not mid-image.
Options.Decode.DemodType.Help: Which FM discriminator algorithm decodes the audio. Hilbert transform matches legacy's own shipped default. PLL and zero crossing are real, selectable alternatives; PLL is also always used internally for AVT training regardless of this setting. Applies live on Save; if a reception is in progress, it queues and takes effect once that reception ends, not mid-image.
Options.Decode.RxBuffer.Help: Stages decoded picture lines so a later sample-rate/sync correction (Auto Slant, or a manual Correct Slant) can redraw already-received lines without re-decoding from scratch. Off disables this entirely -- no correction ever redraws past lines, and Auto Slant is unavailable. On keeps the buffer in memory, bounded by available RAM. Extended stores it on disk instead, with no practical size cap but real disk I/O cost -- best for long or marginal-signal receptions. Applies live on Save; if a reception is in progress, it queues and takes effect once that reception ends, not mid-image.
Options.Decode.AutoRestart: Restart onto a stronger sync mid-reception
Options.Identification.SoundFile.Help: A recorded audio file played instead of a CW-keyed tone for identification -- legacy's own .mmv sound-file ID, not a picture/image ID. Up to 32 MB.
Options.Radio.SoundFileId.Error.BlocksSa: ID sound file can't be saved: {0}
Options.Identification.NrRstEnabled: Send NR/RST sub-packet with FSK ID
Options.Identification.NrRstTextWatermar: e.g. 599123 (static value, not a live QSO exchange)
Options.Advanced.Caption: Deep DSP tuning, ported from legacy's own Option dialog. PLL/zero-crossing rows apply live to the running decoder; TX filter rows apply on the next transmission.
Options.Advanced.PllHeader.Help: Internal filter parameters for the PLL-based FM discriminator -- used whenever "PLL" is the selected picture demodulator (Decode tab), and always for AVT training regardless of that selection.
Options.Advanced.Pll.CutoffWarning: High cutoff values degrade the picture. The PLL demodulator breaks into a herringbone pattern well below the maximum, where the other two only get grainy. Leave these at their defaults unless you are deliberately experimenting.
Options.Advanced.CrossingHeader.Help: Internal filter parameters for the zero-crossing discriminator -- used whenever "Zero crossing" is the selected picture demodulator (Decode tab).
Options.Qrz.QrzLookupPasswordHint: Stored locally, unencrypted -- consider using a unique password for this account rather than one reused elsewhere.
Options.Forwarding.Description: Every logged QSO is sent to each enabled destination below over UDP, using the WSJT-X network protocol's LoggedADIF message -- the same message GridTracker, N1MM Logger+, and Log4OM already know how to receive. Common ports: GridTracker 2237, N1MM Logger+ / Log4OM 2333.
